title: Nat Schwartz joins Whiting and Johnson as a trio
summary: Whiting brought in Nat Schwartz as lyricist; Johnson insisted on credit only for the music.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Ah! Now what about Nat Schwartz? You worked with him, too.
Nat Schwartz, yes, he -- George Whiting brought Nat Schwartz in to make a trio.
See ... George and I were writing, and George brought Nat in as a lyric writer.

So if you'll notice, on any of the songs that are published, you'll see George Whiting and Nat Schwartz, lyric, and music -- J.C. Johnson. See, we got that straight from the beginning; I said, 'Now, I have nothing to do with the lyrics, I'm the tune writer. So I only want credit for what I do, don't want credit for any words at all.' And that's the way it always stayed.
I know that composing is your favorite, I know that that's your real first love, but your lyrics are really extraordinary.
I can write a bit of them, too, you know, when the time comes that you need a lyric here and there, if you've got a good word that fits, throw it out there -- and I always did that.
